主要内容: In March 2013, access to employee benefits varied significantly between private industry and state and local government employees. According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, 64 percent of private industry employees had access to retirement benefits, compared to 89 percent of state and local government employees. Private industry workers were also less likely to have access to medical care benefits and paid sick leave. Among private industry workers, access to benefits varied by the size of the establishment. For example, 45 percent of workers in establishments with 1 to 49 employees had access to retirement benefits, while 87 percent of workers in establishments with 500 workers or more had access. Employer-provided medical care benefits were available to 70 percent of private industry workers, compared to 87 percent of state and local government workers. Paid sick leave benefits were more commonly offered to state and local government workers (89 percent) than to private industry workers (61 percent). These data are from the National Compensation Survey – Benefits program.
